claims.text: A high degree of lattice distortion induces a fine, nanoscale grain structure in lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Chemical heterogeneity induces a fine, nanoscale grain structure in lightweight high-entropy alloys.
The nanoscale grain structure reinforces mechanical strength.
Nanoscale grain boundaries promote rapid formation of a stable, self-healing oxide layer.
The proposed microstructural synergy permits low density to coexist with superior mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Rapid solidification produces a homogeneous, fine-grained microstructure in the lightweight HEA.
The initial fine-grained alloy has significant lattice distortion.
Annealing the alloy promotes grain coarsening without changing its composition.
Lattice distortion and chemical mixing hinder dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion and chemical mixing hinder defect clustering.
Suppression of dislocation motion and defect clustering maintains high mechanical strength.
The chemically heterogeneous, lattice-distorted microstructure facilitates formation of a protective, self-healing oxide layer.
Grain coarsening diminishes the beneficial effect of lattice distortion and slows protective oxide formation.
The as-deposited fine-grained alloy will have higher yield strength than the annealed coarse-grained alloy.
The as-deposited fine-grained alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the annealed coarse-grained alloy.
The as-deposited fine-grained alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the annealed coarse-grained alloy.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure that causes extensive grain growth will cause the proposed mechanism to cease holding.
Deviation from the optimized composition can eliminate the lattice distortion required for rapid self-healing oxide formation.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as homogeneous, while chemical heterogeneity is asserted to be the source of the operative microstructure. These could coexist at different length scales, but no scale distinction is provided.
